comp_micro_degree → comp_meso_component_edge_density upward Fish with many contacts locally increase the number of realized edges within their component, raising meso edge density.

comp_micro_degree → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance upward High-degree fish are surrounded by many close neighbors; their local crowding can lower the mean nearest-contact distance of their component.
comp_micro_degree → comp_macro_school_clustering upward High-degree individuals create more neighbor-neighbor contact opportunities, which can promote triangles and increase global clustering.

comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance upward Individual nearest-contact spacing is the local quantity whose distribution determines the component-level average nearest-contact distance.
comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance → comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance upward School-wide mean nearest-contact distance reflects the aggregation of local nearest-contact distances across fish.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_micro_degree downward A component with higher mean degree offers more potential contact partners, plausibly raising the realized contact degree of a focal fish in that component.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance downward Higher component connectivity can bring neighbors closer or create crowding, plausibly changing a focal fish's nearest contact distance.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_micro_clustering_coefficient downward Component-level contact density can create more neighbor-of-neighbor links, plausibly increasing a focal fish's local clustering coefficient.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_macro_school_clustering upward Components with higher mean contact degree support more transitive contacts, and the mixture of such components can raise school-level clustering.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance upward Components whose fish have many contacts are generally more crowded; when such components dominate, the school-wide mean nearest-contact distance tends to decrease.

comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → comp_meso_component_edge_density intra_scale Larger mean nearest-contact spacing implies fewer close pairs and can lower realized contact edge density within the component.
comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → comp_meso_component_mean_degree intra_scale Looser local spacing can reduce the number of contact neighbors per fish, lowering mean component degree.

comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → comp_macro_school_mean_degree upward Components with smaller mean nearest-contact distances tend to have denser local links, raising school mean contact degree.

comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance upward Component mean nearest-contact distances aggregate across components to determine the school-wide mean nearest-contact distance.
comp_macro_school_mean_degree → comp_macro_school_clustering intra_scale Dense contacts create more neighbor triangles and raise global clustering.
comp_macro_school_mean_degree → comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance intra_scale Higher mean contact degree implies more close contacts, lowering mean nearest-contact distance.

comp_macro_school_clustering → comp_meso_component_edge_density downward Higher global clustering coefficient reflects a more tightly knit contact network, which can locally densify components, raising their edge density.
comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_micro_degree downward When the school is more spread out, individual fish have fewer close contacts, plausibly reducing focal contact degree.

comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance downward School-level spacing sets the local crowding regime, plausibly shifting the nearest contact distance experienced by an individual fish.

comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_meso_component_edge_density downward Larger typical nearest-neighbor spacing reduces the chance of local contacts, plausibly lowering component edge density.

comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance downward A school-wide increase in nearest-contact spacing can propagate into component geometry, plausibly raising mean nearest-contact distance within components.
